Subject: Eval setup & recommended models - FinCo next steps

Hi Sara - great to meet you and Tom on today's discovery call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a FinCo-specific eval running on Redwood:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + answer extraction for regulatory inquiry routing.
- Quality bar: high precision on extracted fields (customer name, account id, issue type) + concise summaries.
- Throughput: ~200 qps peak, mostly sub-second latency requirements for routing.

Recommended models to evaluate (start here):
1) redwood/phi-7b-chat - fast, low-cost baseline; robust for extraction tasks with tuned prompts.
2) open/llama-2-13b-chat (quantized) - higher quality on abstractive summaries, slightly higher latency/cost.
3) rlhf/sft-13b-cust (if you have labeled examples) - fine-tuned option we can host on Dedicated for production.

Eval plan and dataset guidance
- We'll run a customer-specific eval on Redwood using a CSV feedback dataset. Please use the attached finco-eval-template.csv as the starter format (columns: id, prompt, context, expected, label_type). For extraction fields, include a gold 'expected' JSON string of the fields.
- Scoring: exact-match for discrete fields (account_id, issue_code), token-overlap/ROUGE for summaries, and semantic-similarity (embedding cosine >= 0.85) for intent classification.
- We'll provide an initial scoring rubric; SEs (cc'd) can tweak thresholds with you.

Operational next steps
1) You upload a ~200-500 sample rows CSV to the Drive folder I shared (or reply with a sample).
2) Rishi will upload it into a private eval project on Redwood and run baseline models.
3) We'll share a report with per-model metrics, confusion matrices, and example failures.
4) Decide if you want to run a larger ~5k row eval and iterate prompts or pursue fine-tuning.

Links & artifacts
- Eval onboarding guide: https://redwood-inference.app/evals/onboarding
- Shared Drive (sample folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinCoEvalSamples

Attachments: finco-eval-template.csv, redwood-eval-guidelines.pdf

Doable timeline: we can run the first baseline eval within 48 hours of receiving the sample CSV. If that works, can you send a sample by end of day tomorrow?

Thanks -
Marissa

Hi Sara - quick answers and the technical checklist to make the eval smooth.

1) Dataset format recommendation (attached template also sent by Marissa):
- CSV columns: id, prompt, context, expected, label_type
  - id: unique string per row
  - prompt: the customer-facing query text (for extraction tasks, include the extractor prompt)
  - context: optional prior messages or metadata (free text)
  - expected: for extractions, a JSON string {"account_id":"12345","issue_type":"billing"}; for summaries, the gold summary text
  - label_type: one of [extraction, summary, classification]

2) PII / privacy: we can create a private eval project scoped to FinCo under our Private tier. Data will only be accessible to your invited users and Redwood SEs assigned to the project. If you need, we can also run the eval on your Dedicated or Private deployment; Marissa can share a quote for Dedicated capacity.

3) Scoring & thresholds (default):
- Extraction fields: exact-match per field -> precision/recall + overall exact-match rate.
- Summaries: ROUGE-L + human-sampled accept/reject. Pass threshold: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 AND human accept rate >= 85% on sample.
- Classification / intent: macro-F1 >= 0.82 (or cosine similarity on embeddings >= 0.85 if you're using semantic labels).
- Failure examples: we'll flag top-K worst-performing prompts and return the raw model outputs alongside gold labels for manual review.

4) How we run it on Redwood (CLI example):
- Upload dataset: redwood eval upload --project finco-eval --file finco-sample.csv
- Run baseline: redwood eval run --project finco-eval --models redwood/phi-7b-chat,open/llama-2-13b-chat --metrics extraction,rouge,classification --output report_finco_baseline.json

5) Artifacts we’ll share: per-model metrics, confusion matrices, example failures, and a short recommendations doc (prompt tweaks, candidate models, and quantization advice).

Attachments: finco-eval-template.csv (sample rows populated), redwood-eval-guidelines.pdf

I can help import your sample tomorrow and kick off the baseline run - ping me the Drive link or attach the file.

-Rishi
